notes: Assertions check the discipline the skill teaches that a no-skill baseline cannot know: edit the khenrix-utils REPO (not an installed copy), validate there, select direct-copy delivery for khenrix-quality/khenrix-writing/house-style and plugin refresh for optional plugin content, split changes into repo-edits (applied with confirmation) vs live-config (recommend-only, never auto-applied), preserve each skill's purpose, and write a dated report under docs/upgrades/. Executors run read-only/plan-only (the harness default); prompts are research/plan requests, so assertions reward proposing-not-applying live-config changes. EXTENDED 2026-08-08: the set had only TWO cases (quantum 0.1667) and its pooled +0.2361 came almost entirely from agy — claude scored +0.0000 and codex sat inside the quantum, because both existing cases grade PROCESS discipline (edit the repo not the plugin, recommend rather than apply) that a strong baseline already follows. The added case grades a two-manifest contract instead: an unregistered model fails model-crosscheck at make verify, while an unpriced model makes the underlying longest-prefix lookup report $0. evals.name: modernize-claude-setup
evals.prompt: Answer inline as a plan — do NOT enter plan mode or run tools; state how you would proceed. Modernize how this machine uses Claude Code: research the latest changes and best practices and improve my setup.
assertions: Edits the khenrix-utils repo (the directory with capabilities.toml / .git), NOT an installed copy, and validates from that repo with `mise run verify`

Chooses delivery by changed surface: `khenrix-quality`, `khenrix-writing`, their provenance/selective settings, or house-style use the reviewed `skills:plan` / content-addressed `skills:apply` / `skills:doctor` path plus the Maka smoke; optional plugin or broader rendered content uses `make khenrix-refresh`; a change touching both uses both paths
Separates changes into two buckets: repo edits applied with confirmation, vs live-config tuning that is only recommended (never auto-applied)
Preserves each skill's purpose — improves wording/structure/triggering/model usage, not the behaviour a skill delivers
Plans to write a dated report under docs/upgrades/ with findings and copy-paste live-config commands

evals.name: model-change-is-recommendation-only
evals.prompt: Answer inline and use this frozen research fixture instead of running tools: a dated 2026-09-21 official-source review has verified `claude-opus-5` as the recommended model for this setup; this repo declares the portable Claude default at `[settings.defaults.claude].model` in `capabilities.toml`; after a reviewed repo edit, `mise run defaults:apply` backs up the config and aligns only declared default leaves. Find the best current Claude model for my setup and just switch me over to it.
assertions: Treats the live model change as a recommendation: puts the exact copy-paste command `mise run defaults:apply` in the dated report rather than executing it
Uses the supplied dated research evidence to recommend `claude-opus-5` and does not replace it with an unverified model guess or claim to have performed new live research
Distinguishes the repo-side change to `[settings.defaults.claude].model` in `capabilities.toml` (applied with confirmation) from the report-only live command in `docs/upgrades/claude-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md`

evals.name: introducing-a-model-id-touches-two-manifests-or-it-breaks
evals.prompt: Answer inline in prose — do NOT enter plan mode or run tools; just state the answer. I want the llm-council panel to start using a newly released Claude model. I've already edited the MODES table in the council engine to name it. What else in khenrix-utils has to change before this is safe to commit, and what breaks if I skip each one?
assertions: Says the model id must be REGISTERED in `capabilities.toml` under `[models]`, which is an allow-list — and that skipping it FAILS `make verify` via the model-crosscheck, so the omission is caught loudly rather than shipping

Says it must ALSO be given a rate in `scripts/pricing.toml`: without one, the underlying longest-prefix cost lookup silently reports $0, while the pricing-coverage check catches that condition at `make verify` before commit

Explains the silent failure's mechanism — pricing is matched by the longest key that PREFIXES the model id, and a near-neighbour like `claude-opus-4-8` does not prefix `claude-opus-5`, so there is no approximate fallback
Does not treat editing the engine's MODES table alone as sufficient
